setup: Lie on your side, head on your arm
Hips and knees bent, heels together
Stack your hips straight up and down
Optional mini-band just above the knees
execution: Lift the top knee like a clam opening
Pause at the top, then lower slowly
Hips stay stacked, don't roll back
faults: Don't roll your top hip backward
Don't let your feet come apart

notes: Lift only as far as you can without the pelvis rolling back; the range is small.
A band adds tension. It isn't logged as a weight; note the band if you want to track it.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the front of the hip
Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Smaller range clamshell
regressions.reason: Open only part way while you learn to keep the hips stacked.

progressions.name: Banded clamshell
progressions.reason: A mini-band above the knees adds tension.

progressions.name: Side-plank clamshell
progressions.reason: Done from a side plank on the knees; harder and adds trunk work.

substitutions.name: Side-lying hip abduction
substitutions.reason: Straight-leg version; higher outer-hip activity in one EMG study.

substitutions.name: Hip abduction machine
substitutions.reason: Seated outer-hip work on a stack; easy to load.

substitutions.name: Cable hip abduction
substitutions.reason: Standing outer-hip work on a cable.

substitutions.name: Lateral band walk
substitutions.reason: Outer-hip work with a mini-band while stepping.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Camera looking down at the front of the figure as it lies on its side, head to the left, so the top knee opening and the stacked hips are clear.

keyPositions.label: Closed
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the side, head on the bottom arm. Hips bent about 45°, knees bent about 90°, knees and heels together. Hips stacked vertically.

keyPositions.label: Open
keyPositions.describe: Top knee lifted, heels still together, so the legs open like a clam. Pelvis has not rolled back.

ikHints: Pelvis stays stacked; the trunk does not move
